alias:rack::componentlibrary::GrayModule.finding: P2: the record's `implementation` is native/bindings/app/components.cpp, but that file never binds GrayModuleLightWidget (components.cpp:15-39 binds only SCHEMEs, the concrete components and LEDSlider/LEDButton/LEDBezel). The alias is the Python default specialization at src/rackpy/raw/_componentlibrary.py:475 (`_lib.GrayModuleLightWidget = TGrayModuleLightWidget.default()`), and grep of native/ finds it only in registry.cpp comments. The binding and its tests (test_components.py:156-159) are correct. Fix: set the manifest `implementation` (bindings/manifest.json:18) to src/rackpy/raw/_componentlibrary.py.

alias:rack::componentlibrary::RedGreenBl.finding: P2: the only behaviour check is `len(cl.RedGreenBlueLight().base_colors) == 3` (tests/app/in_rack/test_components.py:161). It would pass with wrong colours or a wrong order, and the order decides which lightId each channel reads (componentlibrary.hpp TRedGreenBlueLight adds RED, GREEN, BLUE). The code is correct (_componentlibrary.py:197). Fix: assert `base_colors == [cl.SCHEME_RED, cl.SCHEME_GREEN, cl.SCHEME_BLUE]`.

class_template:rack::componentlibrary::R.finding: P1: the cited test cannot tell RectangleLight from Rack's default circular light. test_rectangle_lights_draw_with_racks_code checks only pixel (5,3) of a 10x6 light (tests/app/in_rack/test_components.py:226, and the layer-1 check after it). Rack's default LightWidget::drawBackground/drawLight draw a circle of radius min(10,6)/2=3 centred at (3,3) (Rack src/app/LightWidget.cpp drawBackground/drawLight), which also covers pixel (5,3). So the test would pass if the Python draw_background/draw_light overrides (_componentlibrary.py:237-266) were never dispatched or drew a circle. test_light_templates_are_specializations does not use RectangleLight. Fix: also assert a pixel inside the rectangle but outside the circle, e.g. (9,3) or (8,1), is 0x33 gray in the background render and lit in the layer-1 render.

class_template:rack::componentlibrary::T.finding: P2: the template's colours are checked only by `len(cl.RedGreenBlueLight().base_colors) == 3` (tests/app/in_rack/test_components.py:161). That would not catch wrong colours or a wrong order (Rack: RED, GREEN, BLUE, which map to firstLightId+0..2). Code at _componentlibrary.py:197 is correct. Fix: assert the exact `[SCHEME_RED, SCHEME_GREEN, SCHEME_BLUE]` list.

class_template:rack::componentlibrary::V.finding: P2: the inheritance differs from Rack's. C++ declares `struct VCVLightBezelLatch : VCVLightBezel<TLightBase>` (componentlibrary.hpp), but the Python class inherits VCVLightBezel's `_bases` → `(_lib.VCVBezel,)` (_componentlibrary.py:401, 415). So `issubclass(VCVLightBezelLatch[BlueLight], VCVLightBezel[BlueLight])` is False, while C++'s is_base_of holds. VCVLightLatch already does this correctly by deriving from `LightButton[VCVButton, arg]` (_componentlibrary.py:376-384). Behaviour (light, latch) is otherwise correct and tested. Fix: override `_bases` to return `(VCVLightBezel[args[0]],)`.

P2: the inheritance differs from Rack's. C++ declares `struct VCVLightSlider : LightSlider<VCVSlider, VCVSliderLight<TLightBase>>`, but the Python specialization's bases are the VCVLightSlider template plus `_lib.VCVSlider` (_componentlibrary.py:330-337). So `issubclass(VCVLightSlider[GreenLight], LightSlider[VCVSlider, VCVSliderLight[GreenLight]])` is False (contrast VCVLightLatch at :376-384). Behaviour (the light follows the handle) is correct and tested. Fix: make `_bases` return `(LightSlider[_lib.VCVSlider, VCVSliderLight[args[0]]],)`, or document the deviation.

P1: neither cited in-Rack test exercises VCVSliderLight's own code. test_light_templates_are_specializations only checks cache identity, `cl.LEDSliderLight[cl.BlueLight] is cl.VCVSliderLight[cl.BlueLight]` (tests/app/in_rack/test_components.py:184), which holds even with an empty class body. test_rectangle_lights_draw_with_racks_code never uses VCVSliderLight. Nothing asserts that it loads Rack's VCVSliderLight.svg (sets sw.svg and a finite box size) or that it is a RectangleLight over TSvgLight (_componentlibrary.py:319-326). Fix: cite test_light_sliders_and_buttons and add, e.g., `assert light.sw.svg is not None and math.isfinite(light.box.size.x) and isinstance(light, cl.RectangleLight)`.

constructor:rack::componentlibrary::Audi.finding: P1: the cited test cannot detect a wrong constructor. test_buttons_and_menus asserts only `b.box.size.x > 0` (tests/app/in_rack/test_io_widgets.py:151-153). Rack's Widget::box defaults to Vec(INFINITY, INFINITY) (include/widget/Widget.hpp:23), and SvgButton sets a size only in addFrame (src/app/SvgButton.cpp:32-43). A plain AudioButton without the ADAT frame would also pass. The binding itself is correct (io_displays.cpp:233). Fix: assert `len(b.frames) == 1`, `b.sw.svg is not None`, a finite box size and `b.shadow.opacity == 0`.

So the test would not fail if Rack's constructor (USB_B.svg frame, shadow opacity 0) did not run. Binding at io_displays.cpp:234 is correct.
